labels.label: schwprop:UnionPasts
labels.notes: schw_prop_2_7 (SchwCausalLemmas.lean:161) states C.Iminus W {γ 1} = ⋃ s ∈ Ico 0 1, C.Iminus W {γ s} for C.ChronalCurveOn W γ 0 1, for any causality C and any open W. With W = ⊤ this is Prop 2.7 (:310–316) once 'future directed timelike curve' is read as a chronal curve, which is the binder's reading. The general Iminus_eq_biUnion_Ico (:142) and its dual Iplus_eq_biUnion_Ioc (:167) are correct generalisations. No hypothesis is added. Prop 2.6 is the axiom isOpen_lt_right, and Iminus is {y | ∃ x ∈ A, lt U y x} (Causal/Causality.lean:101). The row is partial only for the C0 layer 3 (T-loc-c0-metric-causality, which exists in programme/roadmap.toml:2141 and is not done). That is honest. The label is unmarked. Binder localisation [] matches.

labels.label: schwdef:timelike_separated_set
labels.notes: ChronallySeparatedOn W K A B (:368) quantifies over every σ with C.ChronalCurveOn W σ 0 1 ∨ C.dual.ChronalCurveOn W σ 0 1, σ 0 ∈ A, σ 1 ∈ B, and asks for ∃ s ∈ Icc 0 1, σ s ∈ K. That is Def 2.14 (:390–392) word for word, with 'timelike curve' read as future or past directed. Defs 2.1–2.2 (:235–245) force that reading in a time-oriented M, and Def 2.14 is used only on the time-oriented M_int (:1772). Reformulation (:393): schw_def_2_14_iff (:477) takes K closed and C.CausallyArcConnected. That hypothesis is how ETT renders the paper's curve-defined I^± (Def 2.2), so it is a reading, not a silent strengthening. The REPORT and SCOPE disclose it, and it is the binder's localisation causally_arc_connected. ⇐ needs nothing (chronallySeparatedOn_of_Iplus_Iminus). The directions check out: a C.dual curve from A to B gives C.lt V (σ 1) (σ 0), so σ 1 ∈ Iminus V A. Counterexample allRelated_chronallySeparated_not_iff (:518) is genuine: allRelated ℝ is a Causality of the strict library (LineDevelopment.lean:1097), K = {0} is closed, every chronal curve of it or of its dual is continuous, so IVT gives separation, and allRelated's lt on {0}ᶜ relates -1 and 1, so 1 ∈ I⁺(-1, ℝ ∖ {0}). The ⇒ therefore fails without arc-connectedness. This is not a claim against the paper, and none is made. Non-vacuity: timelikeLine_chronallySeparated and timelikeLine_not_chronallySeparated_empty. The label is unmarked and the row is partial.

labels.label: schwthm:MinkInex
labels.notes: Only Step 1's sentence (:485, 'and hence it is future inextendible in M_Mink') is formalized, and the row is partial with that scope stated. futureInextensible_of_leaving (:241) is the universal 'hence': any causal curve of an open U ⊇ W over [a, b], in W on [a, b), with γ b ∉ W, is FutureInextensible in W over [a, b), given [T2Space M], which the paper has as a standing hypothesis (:228). exists_leaving_futureInextensible_of_isOpenEmbedding (:277) adds T2 to exactly the hypotheses of the strict exists_leaving_of_isOpenEmbedding (LocateExtension.lean:418) and adds D.FutureInextensible (range ι) (Ico 0 1) γ to its conclusion. ETT's notion is stated in ι(N) ⊆ M̃, not in N, and SCOPE discloses this. Sbierski's own Def 2.10 sentence in N is not_continuousExtension_preimage (:327): ¬∃ δ' continuous on [a, b] agreeing with δ on [a, b), for any continuous ι. That is literally the paper's notion, so here Lean ≥ paper. futureInextensible_of_not_continuousExtension (:339) correctly proves that Sbierski's notion implies ETT's with no separation axiom. Counterexample forkPoint_leaving_futureExtensible (:631) is genuine. ForkPoint's opens are ∅, {x}, {x,p}, {x,q}, univ, so p and q cannot be separated, and forkPoint_not_t2Space confirms it. toQ is continuous, so it is an allRelated chronal curve of ⊤ over [0, 1]. It lies in xp on [0, 1) and toQ 1 = q ∉ xp, so every hypothesis of futureInextensible_of_leaving except T2 holds. Yet toP over Icc 0 1 with φ = id strictly extends it at the future end by p. Precision point: the witness shows T2 is needed for futureInextensible_of_leaving, the paper's universal sentence. It does not show T2 is needed for the existential exists_leaving_futureInextensible_of_isOpenEmbedding. On ForkPoint with allRelated, all hypotheses of that theorem except T2 hold, and its conclusion is true anyway: the curve p at 0, x on (0, 1), q at 1 already has image {x, p} = ι(N), so it cannot grow. The REPORT's row note ('[T2Space M] … needed …, a curve satisfying every other hypothesis') should be read as being about futureInextensible_of_leaving, as the docstring says (:115). The label is unmarked.
